region.text: Genoa and its Ligurian coast, the Compagna Communis at the end of the 11th century

ledger.note: 1099: Genoa constitutes itself as the Compagna Communis. 'At the end of the 11th century' the city 'adopted a constitution at a meeting of trade associations and local lords' and 'The new city-state was termed a Compagna Communis'; infobox 'Established: 1099', 'from the years 1099 to 1797'. The page gives the year, not the month, and no boundary: the land is the Cliopatria shape of 1099 (Genoa and the nearby Riviera).

By 1200 the whole Ligurian coast is Genoese. 'By the end of the 12th century, all of Liguria fell under the Republic of Genoa.' The page does not date individual towns; Cliopatria draws the extra Riviera cells from 1202. The Holy Roman Empire dossier records a Ligurian loss in 1010; the nominal overlord was the Emperor ('Nominally, the Holy Roman Emperor was overlord').

region.text: the southern tip of Corsica, Bonifacio

ledger.note: 1202: Genoa holds the southern tip of Corsica. Page silent: the History of Corsica page does not mention Bonifacio; the Cliopatria shape adds three Corsican cells in 1202 and the Pisa dossier records the same three leaving Pisa that year. [Repair 2026-10-31: the Bonifacio (Corse-du-Sud) page was opened: it gives the founding of the fortress in 828 by Boniface II of Tuscany and nothing on Genoa, Pisa or 1202; still page-silent.]

region.text: the city and island of Rhodes

ledger.note: 1248: the Genoese seize Rhodes. 'The Genoese took possession of the city and island, a dependency of the Empire of Nicaea, in a surprise attack in 1248' (spring or summer 1248, by 'a Genoese fleet'; the page names no commander and does not say the Republic's government ordered it). Mirror of the occupation in the domain-of-rhodes dossier.

region.text: the city and island of Rhodes

ledger.note: 1248: Rhodes, 'a dependency of the Empire of Nicaea', is attacked; 'Kantakouzenos set out in late 1248 or early 1249'; the Achaean prince arrived 'in about the middle of May 1249'. Mirror of the nicaean-empire contest.

region.text: the city and island of Rhodes

ledger.note: Late 1249 or early 1250: the Genoese surrender Rhodes. 'This took place either in late 1249 or early 1250'; 1250 is taken as the year (the domain-of-rhodes dossier has the eviction in 1250 from the Leo Gabalas page).

region.text: the city and island of Rhodes

ledger.note: Late 1249 or early 1250: the Genoese surrender. The page's own words: 'either in late 1249 or early 1250'.

region.text: north-west Sardinia, the former Logudoro, ruled by the Genoese families of Doria and Malaspina

ledger.note: 1259: the Doria and Malaspina take over Logudoro as Genoese influence. 'The kingdom of Logudoro came to an end in 1259, when the queen Adelasia died without an heir' and 'After this, Logudoro was effectively ruled by the Genoese families of Doria and Malaspina, and the ruling family of Arborea.' The Republic page: 'Genoa had influence over the Giudicato of Logudoro from 1259 to 1325.' The lordships are Genoese families' lands, drawn as a tint, not Genoese territory.

region.text: Caffa (Feodosia), granted to the Genoese in 1266

ledger.note: 1266: Caffa is granted to the Genoese and becomes the capital of Gazaria. 'Caffa was granted to the Genoese' (1266). The page does not name the granting power in the lines read; the Golden Horde ruled the Crimean steppe, so it is the counterpart by my reading. The Republic page says 'In 1255, Genoa established the colony of Caffa' and gives Gazaria from 1266. [Reviewer eu-13-g, 2026-10-31: counterpart changed from golden-horde to ulus-of-jochi, because the golden-horde dossier starts in 1294 and the ulus-of-jochi dossier (1225-1293) is the Jochid state of 1266.]

1275: Chios (with Samos) is granted to Genoa by Byzantium. 'Chios: Granted by Byzantium in 1275 (with Samos)'; the same page also says Genoa controlled it 'from 1261 to 1566', and the Chios page starts Genoese rule with the Zaccaria lordship of 1304. Cliopatria draws the island from 1272. [Repair 2026-10-31: Chios page re-read: authority over the island 'was ceded to the Republic of Genoa (1261)' (Treaty of Nymphaeum) and the page does not mention 1275; the Republic page's 1275 is kept at confidence 2. The same Chios page has the Genoese Benedetto I Zaccaria holding the island from 1304 as 'a renewable concession' from Andronikos II, so Genoa's own hold ends in 1304 (next event).]
1282: Pisa tries to take Corsica from Genoa. 'In 1282, Pisa tried to gain control of Corsica' (the Republic page); the Pisa dossier opens the same contest in 1282.

1284: Genoa takes Elba after Meloria. Elba page: 'After the battle of Meloria, the Republic of Genoa took possession of Elba, but it was regained by Pisa in 1292.' The page gives no year for the possession; 1284 is the year of the battle (Republic page, 5 August 1284). Not in the Cliopatria shape; drawn from this event.

5 August 1284: Genoa wins the naval Battle of Meloria and Corsica passes to it. The month is the battle's date from the Republic page ('On 5 August 1284, in the naval Battle of Meloria'); the History of Corsica page gives the year and the land.

1284: Corsica falls to Genoa. 'it fell to Genoa in 1284, following the battle of Meloria against Pisa.' The Republic page also says Corsica was 'formally annexed in 1347' and 'Under Genoese rule from 1284 until 1768'; the earlier date is kept because it is the one Cliopatria draws (1285).
1292: Pisa regains Elba. Elba page: 'it was regained by Pisa in 1292'.

8 January 1297: François Grimaldi's reign on the Rock begins (List of rulers of Monaco: reign start '8 January 1297'). The page does not say what the Rock was before; the principality-of-monaco dossier has it seized under Genoese sovereignty. Sub-cell. Mirror of the Monaco found event.
10 April 1301: the Rock is back under Genoese control. 'Under Genoese control from 10 April 1301 to 12 September 1331'; François Grimaldi's reign ends '10 April 1301'.

1304: Chios passes from the Republic's own hold to the Zaccaria lordship. Chios page: the island was 'kept as a renewable concession' by 'the Genovese Benedetto I Zaccaria (1304)', who 'made himself ruler'; the page does not make the Zaccaria the Republic's vassals, so the Republic's own hold is ended here at confidence 2 (reviewer's reading, eu-13-g review). The lordship-of-chios dossier (state, 1304-1329) is founded from the Byzantine Empire in this year; it ends in 1329 when the islanders 'expelled the Zacharia family from the island (1329) and dissolved the fiefdom', a change between lordship-of-chios and byzantine-empire in which Genoa has no part (the former 1329 loss to byzantine-empire is deleted).

region.text: the Taman shore of the Kerch Strait

ledger.note: 1305: three cells appear on the Taman side of the Kerch Strait. Page silent: the Gazaria page lists no Taman or Matrega colony in the lines read; the date and place are read from the Cliopatria shape alone. [Repair 2026-10-31: the Matrega page says the Genoese colony 'was canonically established on 1349.02.21 as Metropolitan Archdiocese of Matriga' and 'suppressed around 1400', part of 'a network of Genoese possessions along the northern Black Sea coast'; it gives no date or seller for the acquisition, so 1305 stays a bridge from the shape.]

region.text: the Genoese quarter at Daphnous and the suburbs of Trebizond

ledger.note: 1306: the Genoese and Trebizond fall out. 'After Alexios refused the Genoese demands for further concessions in 1306, they threatened to leave Trebizond altogether'; 'the Genoese set fire to the suburbs of Trebizond'; their settlement 'had outgrown Daphnous, the coastal suburb to the east of Trebizond, and the Genoese demanded more room'. The page does not say whether the Republic or the local Genoese colony was the party. Mirror of the empire-of-trebizond contest.
1308: the Golden Horde takes Caffa. 'The Golden Horde, under Toqta, conquered Caffa after a lengthy siege' (1308). The Golden Horde dossier records the siege from 1307.

1313: Genoa regains Caffa. 'In 1313, having regained possession of the city,' the Republic reorganised its administration, including the Officium Gazarie; the page says the colony was regained five years after 1308.

region.text: the Genoese quarter at Daphnous and the suburbs of Trebizond

ledger.note: 1314: peace. 'Eventually the two parties made peace, confirmed in a surviving treaty from 1314 and another from 1316'; the page does not say who signed.

region.text: La Tana, at the mouth of the Don

ledger.note: 1316: Genoa founds La Tana at the mouth of the Don. 'Between 1316 and 1332, Genoa established the Black Sea colonies of La Tana... and Samsun.' The year is the start of the page's range; the page does not name the granting power (Golden Horde read from the neighbours list). Samsun is not in Cliopatria's shape.
12 September 1331: Charles I Grimaldi 'retook the Rock from the Genoese' (List of rulers of Monaco).

region.text: the island of Chios (the Maona of Chios) and the island of Samos (the Giustiniani)

ledger.note: 12 September 1346: the Genoese Maona takes Chios and holds it as a Genoese chartered company, drawn as a vassal tint of the Republic (the maona-of-chios dossier is type colony, 12 September 1346 to April 1566). Chios page: 'Genoa set up a chartered company, the Maona, to reconquer and exploit Chios and the neighbouring town of Phocaea'; a fleet under Simone Vignoso invaded and the castle surrendered 'on 12 September' (the page gives no year with the date; 1346 is the year of the episode); 'The Maona was controlled by the Giustiniani family' and 'the island remained under Genoese control for two centuries'. Samos is folded into this event: the Samos page says the island, after 'much the same changes of government as Chios', 'became the property of the Genoese family Giustiniani (1346-1566; 1475 interrupted by an Ottoman period)'; this replaces the former 1352 Samos gain (confidence 1, from the Cliopatria shape alone). Phocaea is not in the shape. Replaces the former 1346 gain from byzantine-empire.

1347: the Genoese seize Kerasus. Empire of Trebizond page: 'while the Genoese seized Kerasus', in a passage on the Turkish raids; the only date nearby is 'The years 1347-1348 marked the apex of this lawless period'. The page gives no year for the seizure and no end; the year is bridged from the empire-of-trebizond dossier. The Alexios III page does not mention a Genoese Kerasus.

1349: end of the Genoese hold of Kerasus, bridged: the Empire of Trebizond page gives no end and the Alexios III page links the Genoese only to Leonkastron in 1349; the year is the empire-of-trebizond dossier's.

region.text: Leonkastron, the fort west of Trebizond conceded to the Genoese

ledger.note: 1349: Leonkastron is conceded to the Genoese. Alexios III page: 'The position of Venice had declined following the concession of Leonkastron to the Genoese in 1349'. Year and name are the page's; that it is a fort west of the city is the empire-of-trebizond dossier's reading. Sub-cell.

1354: the Catalans occupy Alghero and the Doria lordships end. Alghero page: 'In 1354, the city was occupied by Catalans'; 'The Dorias ruled Alghero for centuries'. The Republic page puts Genoese influence over Logudoro at 1259 to 1325; Cliopatria's Sardinian cells leave the shape in 1352. The crown of Aragon's Sardinian conquest began in 1323-1324 (Aragon dossier).

1354: the Genoese conquer Tripoli. Banu Thabit page: 'His rule was interrupted by the conquest of Tripoli by the Genoese in 1354-1355.' The page names no commander and does not say whether the Republic or a Genoese fleet acted; 1354 is the first year of the page's span. Sub-cell.

1355: Tripoli is handed to the Banu Makki. 'In the same year, the Genoese agreed to give the city to the Banu Makki, the rulers of Gabes, in exchange for a large payment' (no amount); 1355 is the second year of the page's span.
15 August 1357: 'Under Genoese control from 15 August 1357 to January 1395'; Charles I's reign ends '15 August 1357'.

19 July 1365: the Genoese of Caffa seize Soldaia. Sudak page: 'on 19 July 1365, the Genoese from Kaffa seized the city, which became a Genoese trading colony'; before that, 'in c. 1249 the city came under the control of the Mongol Golden Horde, although it retained considerable autonomy'; 'Genoese rule lasted until 1475' (Ottoman capture by Gedik Ahmed Pasha). The page does not mention Cembalo or Gothia. The Cliopatria shape draws the cell only from 1375 (keyframe 1363 corrected).
1372: Genoa seizes Famagusta. 'In 1372 the port was seized by Genoa and in 1489 by Venice.' Cliopatria's shape has no cell on Cyprus. The Kingdom of Cyprus dossier records the same loss.

region.text: the Kingdom of Cyprus, tributary of Genoa

ledger.note: 1372: the Kingdom of Cyprus becomes a tributary of Genoa. Infobox: 'Tributary state of the Republic of Genoa (1372-1426)'; the kingdom 'dominated more and more in the 14th century by Genoese merchants'. The Republic page's 'Cyprus was granted to the Republic' at the end of the century is not used.

minus.text: the Crimean coast west and south of Caffa, the Gothia coast

region.text: the Gothia coast west and south of Caffa except Soldaia (Cembalo and the rest of the coast)

ledger.note: 1375: the Crimean coast widens to the rest of the Gothia coast (Cembalo; Soldaia has its own 1365 event). The Cliopatria shape adds 5+1 cells in 1375. Page silent: the Gazaria page does not date the Gothia coast, the Sudak page does not mention Cembalo or Gothia, and the Theodoro page calls Gothia 'the Genoese province of Gothia, which comprised the coastal strip from Cembalo to Lusta' without a founding year.

region.text: Genoa and its Ligurian lands under French domination

ledger.note: 1394: the French dominate Genoa. 'After a brief period of French domination from 1394 to 1409'; in 1396 'Charles VI was made the difensor del comune'. Genoa is the occupied party here (the French dossier should mirror it); the page uses 'domination', not 'occupation'.
January 1395: the Genoese control ends 'to January 1395' and Louis Grimaldi reigns from January 1395 (no cause given).
19 December 1395: 'Under Genoese control from 19 December 1395 to 11 May 1397'; Louis's first reign ends 19 December 1395.
11 May 1397: Louis reigns again from '11 May 1397', the Genoese control ending that day.
5 November 1402: 'Under Genoese control from 5 November 1402 to 5 June 1419'; Louis's second reign ends '5 November 1402'.

1405: Livorno is sold to the Republic of Genoa. Livorno page: 'In 1399, Pisa sold Livorna to the Visconti of Milan' and 'in 1405 it was sold to the Republic of Genoa'. The page names no seller and does not mention 1407; Milan as counterpart is my reading from the 1399 sale (confidence 2). Genoa was then under French domination (1394-1409). Not in the Cliopatria shape.
1409: French domination of Genoa ends. 'French domination from 1394 to 1409'; Genoa then 'came under the rule of the Visconti of Milan' (the year of that submission is not on the page).

5 June 1419: 'Sons of Rainier II, Jean, Ambroise and Antoine, bought back Monaco from Genoa' (List of rulers of Monaco). The Monaco dossier notes that the Monaco page itself says the Grimaldi 'purchased Monaco from the Crown of Aragon' in 1419; this entry follows the list page.

region.text: Genoa and the Ligurian coast, ruled by the Visconti

ledger.note: 1421: Genoa passes to Milan. Wars in Lombardy page (footnote): 'Milan controlled Genoa since 1421'; the page does not describe how. The Republic page says only that after 1409 Genoa 'came under the rule of the Visconti of Milan'. The same Wars in Lombardy page has 'Filippo Maria Visconti recognized the independence of Genoa' in the Peace of Cremona of 20 November 1441, against the Battle of Ponza page's 27 December 1435 (see the 1435 gain).

28 August 1421: Florence buys Livorno. Livorno page: 'on 28 August 1421 it was bought by the Republic of Florence' (the page's fortress section says 'bought from Florence', contradicting its own history section).

1422: Aragon holds Corsica. Page silent on the year: the History of Corsica page mentions 'take-overs by Aragon between 1296 and 1434'; the shape keeps only Bonifacio from 1422 and the Crown of Aragon dossier gains Corsica in 1422. [Repair 2026-10-31: Alfonso V of Aragon page: 'Alfonso was also in possession of much of Corsica by the 1420s' (no year); the 1422 date stays a bridge, confidence 1.]
1426: Cyprus ceases to be tributary to Genoa. Infobox: 'Tributary state of the Republic of Genoa (1372-1426)'.

February 1433: Cembalo rises against the Genoese with Theodoro's backing. 'Alexios supported a Greek rebellion in Cembalo in February 1433.' The page does not say the town passed to Theodoro, so it is recorded as a contest, not a loss. The 1423 attack ('the Genoese had to spend a large sum of money to repel him') took no ground on this page; see the war entry.
June 1434: 'A Genoese force reconquered Cembalo in June 1434'; 'Cembalo revolted once more in 1439' (page).

region.text: Genoa and the Ligurian coast, the Milanese garrison driven out

ledger.note: 27 December 1435: Genoa throws off Milan. After the battle of Ponza on 5 August 1435 the Genoese 'started to rebel against him, drove out the Milanese garrison and overthrew his rule on 27 December 1435.' The Duchy of Milan dossier has the Peace of Cremona of 20 November 1441 recognising independence (an unsettled disagreement of six years); Cliopatria returns the core in 1440.

region.text: Corsica except Bonifacio, which stayed Genoese

ledger.note: 1450: Corsica returns to Genoa. Page silent: the History of Corsica page gives no end to the Aragonese holdings (it has the Corsicans' diet at Lago Benedetto in 1453); the Cliopatria shape restores Corsica in 1450 and the Crown of Aragon dossier drops it the same year. [Repair 2026-10-31: the Alfonso V of Aragon page gives no end to the Aragonese hold of Corsica; still a bridge.]

region.text: Genoa and its Ligurian lands as the Duchy of Genoa

ledger.note: 1458: the doge hands Genoa to the French. 'In 1458 the doge handed the Republic over to the French', making it the Duchy of Genoa under John of Anjou. Genoa is the occupied party here.
1461: the Republic is restored after the French handover of 1458.

region.text: Genoa and the Ligurian coast under the Sforza

ledger.note: 1464: Milan conquers Genoa. 'Milan conquered the city, holding it as a fief of the French crown' (1464); 'Genoa was held by the Milanese House of Sforza' in 1463-1478 and 1488-1499 (the page marks these dates 'clarification needed'). The Duchy of Milan dossier records the gain in 1464.

1464: Famagusta leaves Genoese hands. Page silent: neither the Famagusta nor the Kingdom of Cyprus page gives the end of Genoese rule (the Cyprus rulers table gives James II's reign from 1464); the date is bridged from the Kingdom of Cyprus dossier. [Repair 2026-10-31: the James II of Cyprus page never mentions Famagusta's capture or Genoa, and the Charlotte, Queen of Cyprus page has 'In 1460 he [Louis] managed to capture Famagusta and Nicosia' without Genoa; the 1464 date stays a bridge from the Kingdom of Cyprus dossier.]

region.text: Caffa, Kerch and the Don mouth, the Genoese Gazaria

ledger.note: 1475: the Ottomans take the Black Sea colonies. The Gazaria page: the domains were 'conquered by the Ottoman Empire in 1474' (infobox 1471-1475); the Republic page: Gazaria 'from 1266 to 1475, lost to the Ottoman Empire'. The Ottoman dossier adds Kefe in 1475. Since 1453 sovereignty over Gazaria belonged to the Bank of Saint George ('ceded the sovereignty over Gazaria to the Bank of Saint George').
1478: Genoa leaves Sforza rule. 'Genoa was held by the Milanese House of Sforza' in 1463-1478 (the page marks the dates 'clarification needed'). The Duchy of Milan dossier records the loss in 1478.

region.text: Genoa and the Ligurian coast under the Sforza

ledger.note: 1488: Ludovico Sforza's Milan holds Genoa again. 'Genoa was held by the Milanese House of Sforza' in 1488-1499; the Duchy of Milan dossier records the gain in 1488.
1499: the Sforza lose Genoa. The page gives the span end 1488-1499 for the Sforza and 'From 1499 to 1528' for the French occupation; the Milan side is not recorded in the Duchy of Milan dossier.

region.text: Genoa and its Ligurian lands under French occupation

ledger.note: 1499: the French occupy Genoa. 'From 1499 to 1528, the Republic reached its nadir, being under nearly continual French occupation.' Spanish forces 'captured the city on May 30, 1522' during the interval. Genoa is the occupied party here.

1528: Andrea Doria expels the French. 'In 1528, Andrea Doria allied with Charles V to oust the French'; the new constitution of 1528 'made Genoa a satellite of the Spanish Empire' (History of Genoa page).

region.text: Tabarka, off the coast of Tunisia

ledger.note: 1540: Genoa takes Tabarka. 'Controlled by Genoa from 1540 to 1742' (Tabarka, Tunisia). The page does not name the previous holder; the Hafsid sultanate of Tunis is read from the geography. A one-cell island off the Tunisian coast; Cliopatria has no cell for it.

August 1553: a Franco-Ottoman force invades Corsica. 'In August 1553, the Turkish fleet under Dragut...' began the invasion; the Kingdom of France dossier has the same occupation. Genoa is the occupied party here.
1559: France returns Corsica. 'By the Treaty of Cateau-Cambrésis in 1559, the French returned Corsica to Genoa.'

region.text: the island of Chios (the Maona of Chios) and the island of Samos

ledger.note: April 1566: the Ottomans take Chios and the Maona's tint ends. Chios page: 'In April 1566, the island of Chios was captured by the Ottoman Empire' after surrendering to Piyale Pasha; the maona-of-chios dossier carries the loss to ottoman-empire. The Samos page gives the Giustiniani property as 1346-1566. Replaces the former 1566 loss to ottoman-empire.

1580: the Republic styles itself 'Serenìscima Repùbrica de Zêna'. 'Officially, Compagna Communis Ianuensis until 1528, then Serenìscima Repùbrica de Zêna from 1580'; the state, its colour and its dossier continue.

20 August 1713: the Marquisate of Finale passes to Genoa. Marquisate of Finale page: 'the Marquisate of Finale was ceded to the Republic of Genoa on 20 August 1713'; the Finale Ligure page: 'acquired by the Republic of Genoa in 1713', 'confirmed in the possession by the Peace of Aix-la-Chapelle of 1748'. Neither page names the cedent; the last holder either names is Spain ('absorbed by the Kingdom of Spain in 1602'), so kingdom-of-spain is a bridge, to be corrected by the group that holds the 1713 settlement. Explains the one-cell Riviera change of the 1709 shape.
1729: Corsica rises against Genoa. 'In 1729, a full-scale revolt broke out in Corsica.' The rebels had no state until 1755; the later Corsican Republic is named as the counterpart.
1742: Tabarka is lost. 'Controlled from 1540 to 1742'; 'lost to the Bey of Tunis in 1742'.

region.text: Genoa and its Ligurian lands under Austrian occupation and siege

ledger.note: September 1746: the Austrians take Genoa. 'Genoa surrendered to the Austrians in September 1746'; the Austrians returned in 1747 and laid siege to the city. The Republic had declared war on the Kingdom of Sardinia on 26 June 1745.
1748: the Peace of Aix-la-Chapelle lets Genoa keep its lands.
1755: the Corsican Republic is proclaimed. 'In 1755 he proclaimed the Corsican Republic.'

region.text: Corsica except the coastal citadels, held by Paoli's Corsican Republic

ledger.note: 1755: Genoa keeps only the coastal citadels of Corsica. 'The Genoese were penned up in the citadels but ruled nowhere else.' The Corsican Republic dossier takes the island except a few coastal towns.
1767: 'Corsica took the island of Capraia from the Genoese' (Corsican Republic page). Sub-cell.

region.text: Corsica: whatever Genoa still held, the coastal citadels

ledger.note: 15 May 1768: Genoa cedes Corsica to France. Treaty of Versailles (1768) page: 'The Treaty of Versailles was a treaty concluded on 15 May 1768', 'in which Genoa sold Corsica to France' ('Genoa had no option but to put Corsica in pledge to France, to repay its debts'); History of Corsica: 'an open treaty with Genoa ceded Corsica to France in perpetuity', and the Republic page 'forced to cede Corsica to the French in the 1768 Treaty of Versailles'. The treaty page does not mention the coastal citadels. The interior is the Corsican Republic's until its own end.
15 May 1768: the Treaty of Versailles 'established that France would return to Genoa the possession of neighboring Capraia island'. The page does not date the handover; the treaty date is used.

region.text: the Ligurian coast, the Republic's last territory

ledger.note: 14 June 1797: the Republic of Genoa ends. The old elites are overthrown in June and 'the Ligurian Republic was proclaimed on June 14, 1797' under French oversight; infobox 'Disestablished: June 14, 1797'.

wars.name: Genoese venture on Crete (Pescatore and da Costa)
wars.outcome: Enrico Pescatore, 'Count of Malta', took 'large parts of Crete' from 1206; Venice's attack of 1207 failed, but it 'took them until 1212 to evict Pescatore' and 'Only on 11 May 1217 did the war with Genoa end in a treaty that left Crete securely in Venetian hands'.
wars.note: No ledger event: 'Pescatore was largely left unsupported by Genoa' (Kingdom of Candia page) and the Pescatore page calls him a corsair, adventurer and privateer without saying the Commune backed him; the page does not name the signatories of the 1217 treaty. Genoese Chania ('The Genoese held onto Chania') is not dated beyond that. The kingdom-of-candia dossier's contest with republic-of-genoa 1206-1217 reads the Commune into a private venture.

wars.name: Genoese occupation of Rhodes

zones.text: the city and island of Rhodes

wars.outcome: 'The Genoese took possession of the city and island, a dependency of the Empire of Nicaea, in a surprise attack in 1248' and surrendered 'either in late 1249 or early 1250'.

wars.name: Genoese-Pisan war over Corsica (Battle of Meloria)
wars.outcome: Genoa won the naval Battle of Meloria on 5 August 1284 (Republic page) and 'it fell to Genoa in 1284, following the battle of Meloria against Pisa'.
wars.note: 'In 1282, Pisa tried to gain control of Corsica' (Republic page).

wars.name: Genoese-Trebizond dispute over Daphnous

zones.text: the Genoese quarter at Daphnous and the suburbs of Trebizond

wars.outcome: After Alexios II 'refused the Genoese demands for further concessions in 1306' there was fighting ('the Genoese set fire to the suburbs of Trebizond'); peace was 'confirmed in a surviving treaty from 1314 and another from 1316'.
wars.note: The page does not say who signed; no territory changed hands. Kerasus (1347) and Leonkastron (1349) are separate ledger events.

wars.name: Siege of Caffa by Toqta
wars.outcome: The Golden Horde under Toqta conquered Caffa after a lengthy siege in 1308; the Genoese regained it by 1313.
wars.note: The page gives 1308 for the conquest and 1313 for the recovery; the start year 1307 is the Golden Horde dossier's.

wars.name: Genoese conquest of Chios and Phocaea (the Maona)
wars.outcome: A Genoese fleet under Simone Vignoso invaded and the castle of Chios surrendered on 12 September; the Maona, controlled by the Giustiniani, held the island.

wars.name: Siege of Caffa by Jani Beg
wars.outcome: The Golden Horde under Jani Beg 'again besieged Caffa'; the page records no change of hands and links the siege to the spread of the Black Death.

wars.name: Genoese seizure of Famagusta
wars.outcome: 'In 1372 the port was seized by Genoa'; the Kingdom of Cyprus became 'Tributary state of the Republic of Genoa (1372-1426)'.
wars.note: Infobox from the Kingdom of Cyprus page; the page does not describe the fighting.

wars.name: War of Chioggia
wars.outcome: 'The War of Chioggia ended in a Genoese defeat in 1380', which 'pushed it out of eastern Mediterranean markets'.
wars.note: The page gives 1379-1381 and a defeat in 1380; no change of territory is recorded.

wars.name: Theodoro's attacks on the Genoese coast (Gothia, Cembalo)
wars.outcome: 'In 1423 prince Alexios attacked and the Genoese had to spend a large sum of money to repel him'; 'Alexios supported a Greek rebellion in Cembalo in February 1433' and 'A Genoese force reconquered Cembalo in June 1434'.
wars.note: The page does not say that Theodoro kept any Genoese land after 1423 ('it seems that he retained the rest of his conquests' is undefined), so the 1423 gain from Genoa in the principality-of-theodoro dossier has no mirror here.

wars.name: Ottoman conquest of Gazaria

zones.text: the Genoese colonies of Caffa, Kerch and the Don mouth

wars.outcome: The Ottomans 'conquered' the Genoese domains in 1474 (infobox 1471-1475); the Republic page has them 'lost to the Ottoman Empire' in 1475.

wars.name: French occupation of Genoa and Andrea Doria's revolt
wars.outcome: 'Under nearly continual French occupation' from 1499; Spanish forces 'captured the city on May 30, 1522'; in 1528 Andrea Doria allied with Charles V and ousted the French.

wars.name: Franco-Ottoman invasion of Corsica
wars.outcome: A Franco-Ottoman force took Corsica from August 1553; 'By the Treaty of Cateau-Cambrésis in 1559, the French returned Corsica to Genoa.'

wars.name: Ottoman conquest of Chios
wars.outcome: 'In April 1566, the island of Chios was captured by the Ottoman Empire' after surrendering to Piyale Pasha.

wars.name: French-Savoyard invasion of 1625
wars.outcome: 'In May 1625, a French-Savoian army invaded the republic' and was driven out; no territory changed hands.

wars.name: Bombardment of Genoa
wars.outcome: 'In May 1684, as a punishment for Genoese support for Spain, the city was subjected to a French naval bombardment.' No territory changed hands.

wars.name: Corsican revolt and the Corsican Republic
wars.outcome: The revolt of 1729 led to Paoli's Corsican Republic in 1755 and, in 1768, the cession of Corsica by Genoa to France ('an open treaty with Genoa ceded Corsica to France in perpetuity').

wars.name: Genoa in the War of the Austrian Succession

zones.text: Genoa and Liguria, occupied and besieged by the Austrians

wars.outcome: On 26 June 1745 the Republic declared war on the Kingdom of Sardinia; it surrendered to the Austrians in September 1746, who returned and besieged the city in 1747; 'The Peace of Aix-la-Chapelle let Genoa keep its lands' (1748).

wars.name: French conquest of Liguria and the Ligurian Republic
wars.outcome: After Napoleon's army defeated Austria and Piedmont in 1796, the Genoese Jacobins overthrew the old elites in June 1797 and the Ligurian Republic was proclaimed on 14 June 1797.

certainty.note: Communal-era and later frontiers on the Ligurian Riviera are approximate in the pages read, and the overseas holdings (Caffa, Tana, Chios, Corsica's coast) are points and coasts; Corsica fell by battle (Meloria 1284), not by treaty.

Sharp only where a treaty fixes the line: Corsica returned by the Treaty of Cateau-Cambrésis in 1559, Genoa's lands kept at Aix-la-Chapelle in 1748, Corsica ceded by the Treaty of Versailles in 1768. The land frontiers with Savoy, Milan and Parma were not read; a renderer may keep them soft.

sources.note: 'From 1206, Pescatore took control of large parts of Crete'; 'The Genoese held onto Chania'; no word on support from the Commune; 1211 Alamanno da Costa.

sources.note: 'After the battle of Meloria, the Republic of Genoa took possession of Elba, but it was regained by Pisa in 1292'; Appiani of Piombino; 1546 part handed to Cosimo I; no Genoese holding in the 16th century.

notes: Republic of Genoa, written by eu-13-g from 14 pages (the budget for a 38-shape state), the Republic of Genoa article read twice with different questions. START: the page dates the Republic 'from the years 1099 to 1797', so the three Cliopatria shapes of 1010-1098 are marked wrong and the state starts in 1099 (researcher's judgment; the page also has a 958 diploma of Berengar II giving the city 'full legal freedom' and a 1016 defence of Sardinia with Pisa, so a reviewer who wants an earlier city-state could start it there). The Holy Roman Empire dossier (eu-08) has a 1010 loss of the Ligurian coast to Genoa that should move to 1099 or 1200. CLIOPATRIA ROWS THAT NEED CORRECTION (all in keyframe_review): Lesbos and Lemnos are drawn as Genoese 1363-1525 but are the Gattilusio lordship under Byzantium and then the Ottomans (Gattilusio page); Rhodes 1250-1259 not on the Genoa page (other dossiers: 1248 to early 1250); Caffa is missing 1266-1307 and in 1308-1313; Sardinia 1260-1351 is Doria/Malaspina lordship, drawn as a vassal tint; Chios is drawn 1272-1631 but is Genoa's own only 1275-1304 (see the repair pass at the end); the Ligurian core is absent in 1402-1414, 1422-1439 and 1540-1563 (restored); Corsica is absent 1375-1384 (restored) and 1422-1449 (Aragon, ledger); the Black Sea cells run to 1525 but end 1475; Corsica is drawn to 1793 but ends 1768 (interior 1755); the row ends 1795, the Republic 14 June 1797 (new keyframe 1796). SIBLING DISAGREEMENTS: the Battle of Ponza page has the Genoese overthrowing Milan on 27 December 1435; the Duchy of Milan dossier has Milan losing Genoa on 20 November 1441 (Peace of Cremona). The Genoa article's own dates conflict (Caffa 1255 or 1266, Corsica 1284 or 'formally annexed in 1347', Chios 1261 or 1275, Cyprus tributary 1372-1426 or 'granted' in the late 14th century, Sforza dates marked 'clarification needed'). PAGES THAT GAVE NOTHING: Duchy of Milan, Filippo Maria Visconti, Battle of Ponza (a disambiguation page, then the 1435 article); Judicate of Logudoro, Famagusta and Kingdom of Cyprus were thin. NOT REACHED (page budget): Bonifacio's founding (the 1202 Corsican tip is confidence 1), the Maona of Corsica (1378), Smyrna ('In 1261 the city of Smyrna in Asia Minor became Genoese territory', no end date, so no event was written), Phocaea (1346, with Chios), Samos, Samsun and Trebizond/Leonkastron, Pera/Galata ('one quarter of Constantinople', undated), Rhodes 1248-1250, the Genoese Levant quarters (Acre, Tyre, Gibelet, Antioch: no dates after the First Crusade, no cells), the Riviera frontier changes of 1632-1748 (unexplained one-cell shifts, verdict ok, unverified), Finale and Savona, Monaco (the Genoa page has it 'Sold to the Grimaldi family in the 15th century'; the Monaco dossier has it Grimaldi from 1297 under Genoese sovereignty), the Bank of Saint George's takeovers, the 1522 sack and 1527 French return, and the list of doges (identity.rulers omitted: the Genoa page gives only the first doge Simone Boccanegra 1339-1345 and the last, Giacomo Maria Brignole 1795-1797). OVERLORDSHIP: French domination 1394-1409, 1458-1461 and 1499-1528 is written as occupation events from Genoa's side (Genoa the occupied party; the Kingdom of France dossier should carry the mirror, possibly as a vassal tint), Milanese rule as loss/gain pairs that match the Duchy of Milan dossier; the Spanish protection after 1528 ('a satellite of the Spanish Empire', History of Genoa) is not written as an event because Cliopatria and the pages give no date or land beyond that sentence; the Kingdom of Spain dossier may want a vassal_start with this slug. MIRRORS NOT FOUND OR NOT CHECKED (counterpart dossiers by other groups): Golden Horde (Caffa 1266 grant, Tana 1316, Taman 1305, Gothia coast 1375: the Horde dossier has only the 1307-1308 siege), Hafsid Dynasty (Tabarka 1540), Beylik of Tunis (Tabarka 1742), Kingdom of France (the occupations of 1394-1409, 1458-1461, 1499-1528 and the 1768 cession; its Corsica occupation of 1553-1559 is there), Duchy of Milan (no 1499 loss), Byzantine Empire (Chios 1275 only; Samos folded into the Maona's vassal tint from 1346), Ottoman Empire (Chios 1566 is carried by maona-of-chios), Holy Roman Empire (1200 and the 1010 loss, see START). GAZETTEER: names used that the gazetteer lacks: none in the ledger except Tabarka (written as a coordinate); Bonifacio, Caffa (Feodosia), Alghero, Phocaea, Samos, Lemnos and Lesbos (as an alias of Mitilini) are wanted. Specs built from Cliopatria shapes (intersect with Corsica, Sardinia, Crimea, Azov and Kerch) stand in for them. REPAIR PASS 2026-10-31 (after the eu-13-g review): CHIOS is no longer double-drawn. Genoa's own hold is 1275-1304 (loss 1304 to lordship-of-chios, confidence 2; the Chios page has the Genovese Benedetto I Zaccaria holding the island as a renewable concession from 1304 and, separately, authority 'ceded to the Republic of Genoa (1261)'); the 1329 loss and the 1346 gain are gone; 12 September 1346 is a vassal_start and April 1566 a vassal_end of maona-of-chios, whose region also carries Samos (Samos page: Giustiniani property 1346-1566; the former 1352 Samos gain, confidence 1, is deleted); Chios and Samos are subtracted from every keyframe correction 1305-1631. MIRRORS ADDED: Rhodes 1248-1250 (occupation of domain-of-rhodes, contest with nicaean-empire), Trebizond (contest 1306-1314, Kerasus 1347-1349 at confidence 1, Leonkastron 1349), Tripoli 1354-1355, Soldaia 19 July 1365, Livorno 1405-1421, Cembalo contest February 1433-June 1434, Monaco 1297-1419 (nine events), Finale 1713, Capraia 1767-1768, Elba 1284-1292; these sub-cell events are drawn from the ledger, not from the keyframe corrections. NOT MIRRORED, with the page: Crete 1206-1217 (Kingdom of Candia: 'Pescatore was largely left unsupported by Genoa'; war entry only), Elba 1548 (Elba page: Appiani of Piombino, part handed to Cosimo I in 1546, no Genoese holding then; the Florence dossier's 'bought from the Republic of Genoa' is not on the Elba page), the 1423 Gothia 'gain' of Theodoro (page: the Genoese repelled the attack). STILL THIN: Bonifacio 1202, Matrega 1305, Gothia 1375 (Cembalo), Corsica 1422/1450, Famagusta 1464 (pages opened, silent); identity.rulers still omitted (the doge list page gives a partial table).
